payload.feature: Implement decision 0023, Phase 1 — realms: the map is the world, chosen at invocation (docs/decisions/0023-realms.md on main; read it FIRST, it is the accepted ruling; 0019 ruling 10 governs naming, 0021 constraints are explicitly OUT of scope for the v1 schema). Scope: (1) THE MAP: realms.json — a versioned schema contract (a new file beside the frozen ones, the v2-table precedent) with the MINIMAL v1 shape the ruling names: realms (each: name, path, default branch) and the world's journal; nothing more, and the loader refuses unknown fields so v2 additions are a version, not a drift. The BOOTSTRAP map lands at this repository's root listing one realm: this repository, journal .forge/forge.db. (2) --realms <file> on run AND every read surface — run, runs, tui, watch, inspect, export, muninn — defaulting to ./realms.json when present; --db RETAINED and OUTRANKING the map's journal; with neither map nor --db, today's default path behaves byte-for-byte as it always has (a world that never drew a map notices nothing — prove it: existing CLI tests must pass unchanged). (3) PINNED AND EMBEDDED: at run start the engine records the map's content hash into the run manifest and the map content itself into the journal, so the world a run believed in is answerable from the journal alone; a missing or malformed map named by --realms is a refusal before any seat spawns, never a silent fallback. (4) PER-REALM FACTS: the repository facts decisions already record (observed HEAD, drift_detected, dirty_worktrees) are recorded keyed by realm name — one realm today; and the FOLD accepts both shapes: every existing journal (unkeyed facts) keeps folding exactly as it does — prove it against the committed fixture journal and the corpus law (fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson untouched, never regenerated). (5) brokkr realms: a read surface listing the world — each realm, path, branch, current HEAD, and the world's journal; read-only, plain output (0019 law 4; the file is realms.json, the word Yggdrasil appears nowhere in the machine's mouth). (6) NOT in scope: Bifröst contracts, multi-realm runs, per-realm 0021 constraints, any TUI pane work beyond what the existing surfaces need to accept the flag. Frozen contracts stay frozen; event-envelope/v1 untouched (realm keying lives in payload facts, not the envelope). Bundle digests should NOT move in this slice — the map is workspace data, not bundle data; if an unavoidable digest move appears, say why in the commit. CI enforces exact coverage — keep the gate green, and run the full workspace suite untruncated before any result claim.

result.notes: Framed decision 0023 Phase 1 (realms) in .forge/tasks/realms-phase-1.md: add contracts/realms.v1.schema.json (deny-unknown-fields, {realms:[{name,path,default_branch}], journal}) plus a bootstrap realms.json at repo root; thread --realms (default ./realms.json) across run/runs/tui/watch/inspect/export/muninn with --db retained and outranking the map's journal, refusing before any seat spawns on a missing/malformed map named by --realms; pin the map's content hash into a new additive run-manifest version (v1/v3 lineage) and embed the map content into the journal at run start; re-key the existing reviewed_heads/dirty_worktrees/drift_detected facts in engine.rs by realm name while making fold.rs and the drift-check lookup accept both the legacy {"repo":head} shape and the new realm-keyed shape; add brokkr realms as a read-only listing surface. Named exact touch points (crates/forge-cli/src/lib.rs --db/--realms threading across ~16 call sites and the Cmd literals in tests.rs, crates/forge-core/src/dispatch.rs and fold.rs, crates/forge-runtime/src/engine.rs:1284-1302, frozen_contracts.rs). Flagged non-goals (Bifrost, multi-realm runs, 0021 constraints, bundle-digest movement, corpus/phase-machine/frozen-contract bytes) and three open mechanical design calls for the implementer to resolve and record. No production code changed.

Decision 0023 Phase 1 implemented and committed (d3d3f79) on slice-realms. (1) contracts/realms.v1.schema.json publishes forge.realms/v1 beside the frozen files — realms (name, path, default_branch) and journal, nothing more; the loader (forge_core::realms) refuses unknown fields at both levels, a wrong schema tag by name, empty realms/journal, bad or duplicate realm names. The bootstrap map is at the repo root: one realm, this repository, journal .forge/forge.db. (2) --realms lands on run, runs, tui, watch, inspect, export and muninn run, defaulting to ./realms.json when present; --db became Option and outranks the map's journal; with neither, the journal is DEFAULT_DB exactly as before (existing CLI integration tests pass unchanged; the journal-witness test now also refuses realms/realm_facts anywhere in an unmapped run's events). (3) run-manifest.v4.schema.json = v3 + optional realms {source, sha256, map}; Engine::start_in_world pins the map's canonical-JSON digest AND embeds the map into the manifest, which rides inside run/started. bundle_manifest_from_run drops the pin so resume still compares the bundle manifest — no bundle digest moved (witness_digests unchanged). A named map that is missing or malformed refuses before the store is opened or a seat spawns. --dispatch + a map is refused, naming the v2-lineage limitation (the 0016 agents precedent). (4) reviewed_heads is keyed by the realm the repo IS when the map names it, plus a realm_facts input (head, dirty_worktrees, drift_detected) — both engine-owned; forge_core::realms::recorded_head accepts the legacy unkeyed 'repo' key and a single recorded realm, so every existing journal folds as it did (proved against the committed fixture journal in fold_test.rs; fixtures/evaluator/corpus.ndjson untouched and still digest-pinned). (5) brokkr realms lists map, journal and each realm with path, branch and current HEAD — read-only, plain, sanitized through render::Safe. Out of scope untouched: Bifrost, multi-realm runs, per-realm 0021, TUI panes; event-envelope/v1 unchanged. Verified: cargo fmt --check clean, clippy -D warnings clean, cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked green (37 test binaries, 0 failures), both self and verify bundles compile, and the exact-coverage gate's own arithmetic over a fresh cargo llvm-cov --branch run is literal 100%: lines 11741/11741, branches 1774/1774, functions 1042/1042. Known boundary left for the operator: resume/rerun/operator/anchor/costs/compare/replay keep --db alone (the ruling's flag list excludes them), so a run started in a mapped world is resumed by naming its journal.

Reviewed d3d3f79 (the whole delivery; fold.rs/policy.rs/forge-store deltas in `git diff main...HEAD` belong to 0022, already merged). Re-ran the full workspace suite untruncated (`cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked`, exit 0, every `test result:` line ok) and reproduced the exact-coverage gate arithmetic from a freshly generated lcov in this worktree: lines 11741/11741, branches 1774/1774, functions 1042/1042 — 100%, gate green. Frozen bytes are untouched, the corpus is untouched, no bundle digest moved (proved by the compile-vs-export files comparison and by witness_digests being unmodified), and the unmapped path is genuinely inert (witness_journal now refuses `realms`/`realm_facts` at any depth; the committed fixture journal still chains, folds and reads identically). The loader, the dual-shape read, the pin/embed, the per-realm keying and `brokkr realms` all match the ruling, and the tests are honest rather than decorative. No fixes applied — the two mediums are design calls that belong with the implementer, not with a reviewer's patch.

FINDINGS (none fixed):

1. MEDIUM (security — information disclosure). `export --redact` now leaks operator-machine paths through the manifest. crates/forge-cli/src/lib.rs:1149-1166 writes `<run>.redacted.manifest.json` from the RAW manifest with only `redacted`/`redaction` keys added; only the NDJSON goes through `forge_store::redact_export`. Before this slice the manifest carried no environment paths; it now carries `realms.source` (the map file as named at invocation — absolute whenever the operator types `--realms /home/<user>/clients/acme/realms.json`) and the embedded map's realm `path` values (absolute in exactly the multi-project world the ruling exists for). So the published redacted pair disagrees: run/started's embedded manifest inside the .redacted.ndjson is scrubbed to `[path-N]`/`[user-N]`, while the .redacted.manifest.json beside it states the real paths and usernames verbatim — against redact_export's own documented promise (forge-store/src/lib.rs:296-308) that machine detail 'never leaves the machine'. Not fixed here because doing it right means sharing one `PathTable` between the journal and the manifest (otherwise `[path-1]` means two different things in the two files), which is an API change to forge-store plus tests plus the 100% gate — an implementer's change, not a reviewer's.

2. MEDIUM (correctness/regression). `brokkr run --dispatch` is now refused in ANY workspace that merely CONTAINS a realms.json — including this repository's root, as of this slice's bootstrap map. crates/forge-cli/src/lib.rs:944-960 asserts `world.is_none()`, but `world` comes from `world_and_journal`, which auto-discovers `./realms.json` (lib.rs:833-841); the refusal cannot distinguish 'the operator named a map' from 'a map happened to be lying here'. There is no opt-out: `--db` does not affect discovery and there is no `--no-realms`, so the only escape the error text can offer is 'invoke from a workspace with no map' — i.e. leave the repository. README.md:588 documents `brokkr run --dispatch <forge-dispatch-v2.json>` as the Looper-bound entry point, so a documented path regressed to exit 1 in the repo it is documented in. Refusing loudly over dropping a pin silently is the right instinct; scoping the refusal to an EXPLICIT `--realms` (and ignoring an incidental discovered map for a v2-lineage run) would keep both properties.

3. LOW (correctness — ruling 5 degrades mid-run). A resumed run stops keying facts by realm. `Engine::resume` sets `world: None` (engine.rs:234-240), so after `brokkr resume` the same run records `reviewed_heads` under the legacy `repo` key and emits no `realm_facts` at all — the journal changes fact-shape mid-run depending on which verb was typed. Nothing breaks (the dual-shape `recorded_head` keeps the ship gate's drift check, which is tested), but ruling 5's 'recorded per realm, keyed by realm name' quietly stops holding, and the information needed to hold it is already pinned in the run's own manifest (`realms.map`), which resume reads anyway. Rehydrating the realm from the pin rather than defaulting to the legacy key would close it.

4. LOW (contract fidelity). contracts/run-manifest.v4.schema.json describes itself as "v3's bytes plus one optional 'realms' property", but its `agents` property is reduced to `{"type":"object","minProperties":1}` with a prose note, dropping v3's full per-invocation-site sub-schema (required keys, digest patterns, the closed `skipped.reason` vocabulary, the `notices` shape). A consumer validating a manifest against v4 therefore gets materially weaker guarantees than against v3, in a file whose stated purpose is that it is v3 plus one field.

5. INFO (scope). `brokkr realms` has no `--json`. The ruling (0023 ruling 6) does not require it and this phase's task text says 'plain output', so this is not a defect — but the run's own framing (.forge/tasks/realms-phase-1.md) listed `--json` under both 'Files expected to change' and 'Tests that must prove this', so it is a silent narrowing of the framed scope rather than a recorded design call. Worth an explicit yes/no rather than an omission.

6. INFO (test fragility). crates/forge-cli/src/tests.rs::the_map_names_the_journal_and_db_outranks_it and ::the_realms_verb_reads_the_world_or_says_there_is_none assert on process-CWD discovery (`world_and_journal(None, None)` must find no world). They pass only because cargo sets the CWD to the crate directory; run from the workspace root — which now carries realms.json — both fail. Pointing discovery at a tempdir, or making the discovery directory a parameter, would make them independent of where the harness stands.

7. INFO (security — matches existing idiom, noted not charged). Refusal text interpolates untrusted map content straight to the terminal: `RealmsError::Invalid` embeds the file's `schema` value and `RealmsError::Malformed` embeds serde's message (which quotes the offending field name), and forge_cli::main prints it with a bare `eprintln!("error: {e:#}")` — no `render::Safe`, so ANSI/bidi sequences in a realms.json survive to the tty. This is the pre-existing idiom for every workspace file the CLI reads (CompileError et al. do the same), so it is not new; what is new is that realms.json is the first such file read by CWD auto-discovery rather than by explicit naming, which widens who can put text on the operator's terminal by one step (`cd` into an untrusted clone, run any read surface). Same step admits an attacker-chosen journal path (SQLite create at an arbitrary path) and an attacker-chosen git working directory for `brokkr realms`. All of it is the accepted ruling's own default-discovery design, and none of it rises past info on this codebase's threat model, but it is the trust boundary that moved in this slice and should be a conscious operator ruling rather than an accident.

FIXES APPLIED (commit 91a157d, one commit, no engine/contract/digest behaviour changed, suite re-run green): (1) `export --redact` now scrubs the manifest through the same Redactor as the journal — correct, and what lets the pair be published — but scrubbing rewrites the realm paths inside the embedded map while realms.sha256 stays the digest of the map that was actually in effect (crates/forge-cli/src/tests.rs:383 asserts exactly that). A reader who checks the pin therefore gets World::from_manifest's tamper wording ("the embedded map hashes to X, not the pinned Y") for what is only redaction. Recomputing the digest would be worse — it would forge a pin for a map no run believed in — so the fix is declaration: the redacted manifest's `redaction.hashes` now names the realms pin beside the event-hash caveat it already carried, `redaction.scheme` no longer claims only "event payload string fields" are rewritten, and a new assertion pins both the mismatch and the declaration. (2) README: one paragraph saying Phase 1 wires --realms into run and the seven named surfaces only, so an operator whose map names a non-default journal knows to pass --db to `resume`/`rerun` rather than meeting it as a run that cannot be found.

RESIDUALS (not fixed; both are design questions for the table, not defects I should decide alone):

[low, SECURITY] Ambient map adoption is silent, and it creates files. World::discover picks up ./realms.json with no --realms typed (ruling 3 mandates this), and Store::open does `create_dir_all(parent)` before opening — so a realms.json that appears in the working directory silently moves where the next `brokkr run`/`runs`/`inspect`/`export` creates directories and a sqlite journal, at any operator-writable absolute path the file names, with no stderr line stating the journal actually opened. The relevant threat model is the self-forge loop itself: a seat has write access to this repository and could plant or edit realms.json between runs. I rate this LOW rather than medium because it is not an escalation — a party who can write realms.json can also write bundles/self/*, which the next run compiles and executes as driver commands, i.e. they already have strictly more than journal redirection — and because sqlite refuses to open a non-database file, so existing content is not overwritten. What is missing is notice, not a guard: the implementation already carries `Invocation.named` distinguishing a typed map from an ambient one (it is used to refuse --realms with --dispatch, and to print a note when an ambient map goes unpinned), so if the table wants it, one stderr line naming the resolved journal when an unnamed map redirects it is the whole fix. INFO detail in the same area: in the Cmd::Run arm the `--dispatch` + `--realms` refusal (crates/forge-cli/src/lib.rs) fires after Bundle::compile and Store::open, so that particular refusal creates the journal before refusing. The refusal the framing actually required — a missing or malformed map — does fire first, before any store is opened, and crates/forge-cli/tests/realms.rs:294 proves it by asserting nothing was written at all.

[low, correctness/simplicity] forge_core::realms::recorded_head accepts a THIRD shape the ruling did not ask for. The ruling requires two: realm-keyed, and the legacy unkeyed `repo` key. The implementation adds a fallback where a record holding exactly one entry answers for whatever realm it is asked about, under any name. Its stated justification — "brokkr resume takes no map" — no longer holds in this same slice: Engine::resume rehydrates the world from the manifest pin (engine.rs:239), so a resumed run does know its realm. Impact today is genuinely low: the len()==1 guard means it cannot fire once several realms are recorded, and a wrong-realm match would compare mismatched HEADs and so report drift_detected=true, which is fail-closed. But it is lenience the ruling did not rule, in the one function that feeds the ship gate's drift check, and it should be revisited before Phase 3 multi-realm runs rather than inherited.

No security finding rises to medium, high or critical, and nothing here weakens fail-closed behaviour: realm_facts was correctly added to ENGINE_OWNED_INPUTS so no seat may declare or claim it, realm names are validated to [a-z0-9._-] before becoming journal keys, realm paths and branches are escaped through Safe in the text readout and left verbatim only in --json, World::from_manifest re-derives the pin's digest and re-validates the map by the same rules that admitted it and refuses on either failure, and bundle_manifest_from_run drops the realms key only for the local lineage, where a bad map then refuses at resume rather than being ignored.

Three residuals, none fixed by me (the first two are policy-gate / operator-ruled territory, not reviewer-safe edits):

1. MEDIUM (security — fail-closed weakening). crates/forge-runtime/src/engine.rs:1348-1356 with forge_core::realms::recorded_head. In a mapped world the ship phase computes `drifted` as `state.reviewed_heads.and_then(|r| recorded_head(r, realm))` and inserts `drift_detected` only when that is Some. If the protected phase recorded `{"<realm>": head}` and the ship phase's `--repo` no longer resolves to a mapped realm (realm = None), `recorded_head` returns None — the keyed entry is not consulted and the legacy `repo` key is absent — so `drift_detected` is OMITTED entirely. policy/phase-machine.json SHIP-DRIFT matches only `when: {drift_detected: true}`, so an omitted input is indistinguishable from clean and the run falls through to SHIP-OK. Concretely: `brokkr run --repo <realm tree>` gets through review and parks; `brokkr resume --repo <a different tree>` reaches ship; before this slice that produced `drift_detected: true` and re-armed review, and now it produces silence. ac3bbdb's ruling 2 deliberately chose "an unnamable realm yields no head rather than one from the wrong tree", which is defensible, but it did not address the consequence at the gate: a fail-closed reading would insert `drift_detected: true` (or park) when a reviewed head exists that cannot be matched to the current realm, rather than dropping the input. No test covers this shape — `realm_facts_state_only_what_the_tree_answers` (engine/tests.rs:2207) asserts the absence only for the case where NOTHING was reviewed. Mitigating: SHIP-DRIFT is `flagged`, not `hard`, and its own reason names forge-control.py's live `ship_gate()` as the fail-closed authority (that file is not in this repository), so this is a loss of a secondary re-arm, not of the last line.
